questions.q: Find the mean of $4,8,6,10,7$.
Find the median of $3,9,5,1,7$.
Find the mode of $2,4,4,6,8,4,2$.
questions.answer: $4$ appears three times, more than any other value, so the mode is $4$.

questions.q: A data set has values $8,12,10,15,10,14,11$. Find the mean, median, and mode.
questions.answer: Sum $=80$, mean $=\dfrac{80}{7}\approx11.43$. Sorted: $8,10,10,11,12,14,15$; median (4th value) $=11$. Mode $=10$ (appears twice).

questions.q: Find the range of $5,12,8,20,3$.
For the data set $2,4,5,7,8,9,12$, find $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.
questions.answer: Median (4th value) $=7$. Lower half $2,4,5$: $Q_1=4$. Upper half $8,9,12$: $Q_3=9$.

questions.q: Find the interquartile range (IQR) for the same data set.
Find the variance of $2,4,6,8,10$, using $\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum(x-\mu)^2}{n}$.
Find the standard deviation of the same data set, rounded to two decimal places.
A data set has variance $25$. State its standard deviation.
A frequency table shows value $1$ with frequency $3$, value $2$ with frequency $5$, and value $3$ with frequency $2$. Find the mean.
Using the same frequency table, find the mode.
questions.answer: Value $2$ has the highest frequency ($5$), so the mode is $2$.

questions.q: Using the same frequency table, find the median.
questions.answer: There are $10$ values in order $1,1,1,2,2,2,2,2,3,3$. Median $=\dfrac{2+2}{2}=2$ (average of the 5th and 6th values).

questions.q: A fair six-sided die is rolled. Find $P(\text{number}>4)$.
A bag contains $5$ red and $3$ blue marbles. Find $P(\text{blue})$.
A card is drawn from a standard 52-card deck. Find $P(\text{king})$.
Two fair coins are flipped. Find $P(\text{both heads})$.
If $P(A)=0.35$, find $P(\text{not }A)$.
A die is rolled. Events $A=\{\text{even}\}$ and $B=\{\text{rolling a }5\}$. Are $A$ and $B$ mutually exclusive?
If $P(A)=0.4$ and $P(B)=0.25$, and $A,B$ are mutually exclusive, find $P(A\text{ or }B)$.
Two independent events have $P(A)=0.6$ and $P(B)=0.5$. Find $P(A\text{ and }B)$.
A fair coin is flipped twice. Find $P(\text{first heads and second tails})$.
A card is drawn from a deck, replaced, then a second card is drawn. Find $P(\text{both are aces})$.
In a class, $P(\text{math})=0.7$ and $P(\text{physics and math})=0.4$. Find $P(\text{physics}\mid\text{math})$.
A box has $10$ balls: $6$ red and $4$ blue. Two balls are drawn without replacement. Find $P(\text{2nd is blue}\mid\text{1st is blue})$.
questions.answer: After removing one blue ball, $3$ of the remaining $9$ balls are blue: $P=\dfrac{3}{9}=\dfrac{1}{3}$.

questions.q: Given $P(A)=0.5$, $P(B)=0.3$, $P(A\text{ and }B)=0.15$, find $P(A\mid B)$.
In how many ways can $4$ books be arranged on a shelf?
How many ways can a committee of $3$ be chosen from $8$ people (order doesn't matter)?
A code uses $3$ distinct digits from $0$–$9$, where order matters. How many possible codes are there?
For the data set $6,10,14,18,22,26,30$, find the five-number summary (minimum, $Q_1$, median, $Q_3$, maximum).
Find the IQR for the same data set.
Outlier boundaries are $Q_1-1.5\times\text{IQR}$ and $Q_3+1.5\times\text{IQR}$. Find both boundaries for the same data set.

sections.heading: Word problems: statistics and probability in context

questions.q: This question has two parts. A survey of $200$ students found that $120$ like math and $90$ like science, while $50$ like both subjects.
parts: Find the probability that a randomly selected student likes math or science, using $P(M\cup S)=P(M)+P(S)-P(M\cap S)$.
Find the probability that a student likes neither subject.

questions.q: This question has two parts. A quality-control inspector finds that $2\%$ of items from a production line are defective. A random sample of $3$ items is tested, and defects occur independently.
parts: Find the probability that all three items are defective.
Find the probability that none of the three items are defective.
